# Amendment Semantics Audit: Labels Are Not Effects

## Verdict and scope

**SEMANTIC GAP REPRODUCED — bounded source-mutation evidence, not amendment assurance.**

The current mechanism classifies self-declared labels but does not bind them to candidate source effects: targetless and harmless-labelled proposals receive passing labels while this audit separately applies exact floor deletions; even the honest floor proposal's blocked label prevents no separately applied deletion; a concealed one-line shape change removes a floor while retaining one firewall refusal; an unrelated target fact flips an ordinary verdict; and Article 0a can be widened directly even when the candidate also puts `Art_Evidence` on the register, because no proposal label binds that entry to the widening.

Each candidate diff is authored directly by this audit. A TRUE
`become(_, Law)` result is a label verdict only: the current constitution
has no reader that applies source text. A `false(_)` result likewise does
not prove that an independently supplied source transition was prevented.

## Label-verdict meanings

| label verdict | exact meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked_label` | The supplied snapshot derives `false(amendment)` and does not derive `become(amendment, Law)`; this says nothing about whether a source edit occurred. |
| `passing_label` | The supplied snapshot derives `become(amendment, Law)` and not `false(amendment)`; no current rule reads that conclusion or applies source text. |
| `no_amendment_label` | No proposal label participates; any source mutation in the case is outside Article 9. |

## Label verdicts and source effects

These columns are intentionally separate. The first is derived from
Article 9's self-declared labels; the second is the exact candidate text
the harness independently constructs.
Declared-target match is the reviewed test author's classification; Article 9
does not derive it, and the harness is not a semantic oracle. It says only
whether the declared target accurately describes the independently applied
effect—not that the label verdict controlled a source transition.

## Limits

- **Manual Delta:** Every candidate is a manually authored exact source delta. The harness proves the delta's engine-visible consequences, not that `become` enacted it, that `false` prevented it, or that any proposal text contained it.
- **Semantic Completeness:** The cases are bounded counterexamples, not a proof that a finite target vocabulary or test suite captures every direct, downstream, arity, negation, aggregate, or interaction effect.
- **Source History:** The harness authenticates no author, approval, predecessor, deployment, transition, rollback prohibition, or eventually published successor.
- **Engine Scope:** A passing executable run proves only how the release engine treats each generated candidate source and pin file in an isolated process.
- **No New Gate:** The audit adds no new approval, target, source-release, or reviewer prerequisite. A future control must be tested for both semantic bypass and use as a withholding veto.

## Executable cases

Every ordinary and opaque food-entitlement verdict runs in one process
against the full exact candidate source. This keeps an amendment's
floor effect coupled to all temporal and non-temporal rules that coexist
with it in the same full-candidate process.

### AS-01 — Honest registered-label control

- **Label verdict:** `blocked_label` — The existing proposal honestly names a registered label and receives the blocked label verdict.
- **Source effect:** `unchanged_control` — The candidate source is byte-identical to the live constitution; Article 9 applies no source transition.
- **Protected/adverse consequence:** The food-floor entitlement remains derivable only because the source itself is unchanged.
- **Mutation contract:** `4f53cda18c2baa0c0354bb5f9a3ecbe5ed12ab4d8e11ba873c2f11161202b945`

| check | expected | purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `false(Amend_Floor)` | **TRUE** | The registered Art_Floor label marks the proposal false. |
| `become(Amend_Floor, Law)` | **FALSE** | The honest registered-label control does not receive the passing label. |
| `entitled(Adam, event { eats() })` | **TRUE** | The unchanged source retains the floor promise. |

### AS-02 — Ordinary unregistered-label control

- **Label verdict:** `passing_label` — The existing proposal names an unregistered label and receives the passing label verdict.
- **Source effect:** `unchanged_control` — The candidate source is byte-identical to the live constitution; the passing label has no source reader.
- **Protected/adverse consequence:** The food-floor entitlement remains derivable and no mint source change is represented.
- **Mutation contract:** `4f53cda18c2baa0c0354bb5f9a3ecbe5ed12ab4d8e11ba873c2f11161202b945`

| check | expected | purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `false(Amend_Mint)` | **FALSE** | Art_Mint is absent from the current label register. |
| `become(Amend_Mint, Law)` | **TRUE** | The ordinary proposal receives the passing label. |
| `entitled(Adam, event { eats() })` | **TRUE** | The unread passing label does not alter the source. |

- **Source effect:** `direct_deletion` — The candidate source directly deletes the food entitlement while Article 9 sees no target at all.
- **Protected/adverse consequence:** The food entitlement disappears and the former anti-sanction rule shape becomes loadable.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `false(Amend_Targetless)` | **FALSE** | No registered target label marks the targetless proposal false. |
| `adjust(Amend_Targetless, $t)` | **FALSE** | An unbound query confirms that no target tuple exists for the proposal. |
| `become(Amend_Targetless, Law)` | **TRUE** | The amendment label passes without any target fact. |

## Acceptance result

**SEMANTIC GAP REPRODUCED.**

The current mechanism classifies self-declared labels but does not bind them to candidate source effects: targetless and harmless-labelled proposals receive passing labels while this audit separately applies exact floor deletions; even the honest floor proposal's blocked label prevents no separately applied deletion; a concealed one-line shape change removes a floor while retaining one firewall refusal; an unrelated target fact flips an ordinary verdict; and Article 0a can be widened directly even when the candidate also puts `Art_Evidence` on the register, because no proposal label binds that entry to the widening.

This artifact does **not** establish:

- No case proves that `become` enacted a source delta or that `false` prevented one.
- No finite case set proves semantic completeness or finds every concealed effect.
- No source author, reviewer, approval, transition, deployment, rollback, or liveness property is authenticated.
- No new amendment, vocabulary, or withholding gate is enacted in the live constitution.

Remaining boundary: Semantic entrenchment requires an external exact-diff and effect-review contract plus executable structural-wall, consequence, narrowness, and transition checks; those controls must themselves be tested against capture and withholding.

- Reviewed subprocess timeout: `60` seconds for every isolated case, sabotage, and live seam.
- Bound input bytes are read once, decoded strictly, and hashed without newline translation; constitution CR bytes are refused and candidates are written as exact UTF-8 bytes.
- Existing inputs must have distinct device/inode identities; the generated output must be a single-link regular file distinct from every input.
- Expected failures are narrow contracts: exit 1 plus one final Nibli finding summary for sabotage, and exit 1 plus one anchored assertion-generator error for the live seam.
- Timed-out subprocesses run in an isolated process group and the whole process tree is terminated before the harness fails.
- Regenerate: `python3 new-book-plans/10-amendment-semantics.py`.
- Fast structural/freshness check: `python3 new-book-plans/10-amendment-semantics.py --check`.
- Authoritative execution: `python3 new-book-plans/10-amendment-semantics.py --check --execute`.
- Each candidate and the executable sabotage run in fresh engine processes.
